note.p: IMPORTANT. This file replaces the project's former Kanchipuram sample corpus with a demonstration corpus for the Halasya Mahatmya / Tiruvilaiyadal Puranam pair. Two things are real here and one is not:

Real: the adhyaya numbering and each chapter's Sanskrit title (head) were read from the OCR'd विषयानुक्रमणिका (table of contents) of the S.V. Radhakrishna Sastri edition digitised on archive.org — see . The OCR recovered legible titles for 62 of the work's 71 adhyayas; the 44 encoded here are the subset the research pass could confidently match to a Tamil padalam. The @corresp links to tiruvilaiyadal-puranam.xml record that matching.

Not real: the exact archive.org item identifier/URL was not retained during the research pass and must be re-found and attached to before this citation is treated as complete. The verse text inside each lg is synthetic placeholder material, a short generic invocatory couplet reused across chapters to exercise the encoding model — it is not a transcription of any adhyaya's actual content and must not be cited as one. See encoding guidelines, section "Replacing the sample corpus".

Adhyayas 1-4 (invocation/kshetra-glorification frame material) and the अनुबन्धः appendix after adhyaya 71 (unrelated hymns) are deliberately excluded from this corpus as non-narrative. Adhyayas 70-71 fall after the point where the Tamil 64-story cycle ends and have no confirmed Tamil counterpart, so are also excluded. Adhyayas with OCR-illegible titles (3, 4, 11, 19, 20, 23, 26, 34, 37, 59, 61) are absent rather than guessed at; a second pass against archive.org's page-image viewer, rather than its plain-text OCR layer, would be needed to recover them.

projectDesc.p: Demonstration of a TEI-based editorial pipeline for South Indian temple legends, built to illustrate eXist-db, RESTXQ, XSLT and Linked Open Data integration.

prefixDef.p: References of the form authority:place-madurai resolve to entries in the shared authority file.

normalization.p: All Indic text is stored in Unicode NFC. Devanāgarī is the storage script for Sanskrit; IAST transliteration is generated, not hand-keyed.
